result.topic_en: Calculations for a new orbital hypothesis for the comet of 1772 that makes its perihelion distance agree with that of the comet of 1805, together with brightness (Lichtstärke) values and derivations of formulas relating true and eccentric anomalies, radii vectors and the parameter of a conic orbit.

1) $\sin\frac12\varepsilon^2 = \frac{rr'\gamma\gamma}{pp[-...-]}\sin\frac12\delta^2$
2) $\cos\frac12\delta\cos\frac12\varepsilon + \frac{\sin\frac12\delta\sin\frac12\varepsilon}{\gamma} = \frac{\sqrt{\frac{r'}{r}}+\sqrt{\frac{r}{r'}}}{2}$
3) $u\sqrt{p} = rr'\sin\delta + pp\gamma^3(\varepsilon - \sin\varepsilon) = pp\gamma^3(\varepsilon + e\sin E' - e\sin E)$

[-$\cos\frac12\delta\cos\frac12\varepsilon \ldots \frac{p}{\sqrt{rr'}}\cos\frac12\varepsilon \ldots$-]
$\cos\frac12\delta\cos\frac12\varepsilon = \frac12\left(\sqrt{\frac{r}{r'}}+\sqrt{\frac{r'}{r}}\right) - \frac{\sqrt{rr'}}{p}\sin\frac12\delta^2$

Aus 2) folgt $\frac{\sin\frac12\varphi^2\sin\frac14(\delta+\varepsilon)^2 - \cos\frac12\varphi^2\sin\frac14(\delta-\varepsilon)^2}{\cos\frac12\varphi^2 - \sin\frac12\varphi^2} = \frac14\left\{\left(\frac{r'}{r}\right)^{\frac14} - \left(\frac{r}{r'}\right)^{\frac14}\right\}^2$
$\frac{\cos\frac12\varphi^2\cos\frac14(\delta-\varepsilon)^2 - \sin\frac12\varphi^2\cos\frac14(\delta+\varepsilon)^2}{\cos\frac12\varphi^2 - \sin\frac12\varphi^2} = \frac14\left\{\left(\frac{r'}{r}\right)^{\frac14} + \left(\frac{r}{r'}\right)^{\frac14}\right\}^2$
$\tang\frac12\varphi^2 = \frac{\left\{\left(\frac{r'}{r}\right)^{\frac14} - \left(\frac{r}{r'}\right)^{\frac14}\right\}^2 + 4\sin\frac14(\delta-\varepsilon)^2}{\left\{\left(\frac{r'}{r}\right)^{\frac14} - \left(\frac{r}{r'}\right)^{\frac14}\right\}^2 + 4\sin\frac14(\delta+\varepsilon)^2} = \frac{\sqrt{\frac{r'}{r}}+\sqrt{\frac{r}{r'}} - 2\cos\frac12(\delta-\varepsilon)}{\sqrt{\frac{r'}{r}}+\sqrt{\frac{r}{r'}} - 2\cos\frac12(\delta+\varepsilon)}$
